test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-idn-002/Biolog.Features.PersonProfileRegistry.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/quality.sh
summary: Closes Seyi's round-1 QA-01 High finding: AssignAsync validated person_id syntax only and never proved the PERSON existed in the resolved tenant, so a probe could assign (and permanently audit) a profile for a wholly synthetic person id, or let a tenant-B caller attach its own profile data to a real tenant-A person id. Fixed with a narrow, read-only gateway rather than a broad coupling: new Domain/IPersonExistenceGateway.cs (a one-method boolean interface this project owns, no ProjectReference to BIO-IDN-001's project), implemented in api/Biolog.Api/Modules/BioIdn002Module.cs by wrapping BIO-IDN-001's own already-registered, tenant-scoped PersonService.GetAsync directly - the adapter gets BIO-IDN-001's own tenant scoping for free since both modules resolve from the same scoped DI container per request. AssignAsync now calls the gateway before the lock and before any audit write; missing and foreign-tenant identifiers return the identical person_not_found (404), matching ADR-0001 SS1.5's no-enumeration-oracle rule. Documented in the README as a correction to the original design's mistaken generalisation of BIO-TEN-002's precedent (control-plane tenant existence is a labelling detail; PERSON's existence is the entire premise a profile depends on - the two pairings are not the same shape).
notes: Verified end-to-end: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api clean (0 warnings/errors). 47/47 feature-local tests (2 new: wholly-unknown-person rejection, fail-closed/no-audit/nothing-stored proof). 154/154 dotnet unit tests (unaffected). 59/59 dotnet integration tests (57 pre-existing + 2 new through the real packaged host: an unknown canonical person id rejected, and a real tenant-A person rejected when referenced through tenant B's verified host - the exact scenario the review's own compiled probe used, now proven closed through the real production adapter, not an injected double). 48/48 offline structural checks (6 new QA-01 checks). dotnet vulnerability audit clean. contract-freeze PASS. traceability PASS. module-project-reference-direction PASS (IPersonExistenceGateway still requires no cross-feature ProjectReference). Full scripts/quality.sh (repo-wide gate): QUALITY: PASS, 0 failures.
